title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1967-11-11
lineage: MSR > R > R > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a fiery 1967 show, highlighted by blazing 'Schoolgirl', soaring Lovelight solos and a monster 'Death Don't Have No Mercy' jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as one of the best‑sounding 1967 tapes, with crisp early tracks and only slight muddiness in the latter half. Musically the band is on fire – Pigpen’s organ solo, Jerry’s incendiary lead work on Lovelight, and extended jams on Schoolgirl, Death Don't Have No Mercy, Cryptical Envelopment and New Potato Caboose receive unanimous acclaim.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars, lauding both the performance and the soundboard quality; minor sound issues are noted but do not detract from an overall exceptional show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early tracks (1‑4) are described as premium/crisp; later tracks (4‑7) become a bit muddy or funky, but overall the sound is outstanding and clean for a 1967 SBD.

standout_songs: That's It For The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with high energy, featuring extended jams and strong transitions; early songs shine brightly while later numbers retain momentum despite minor audio blemishes.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Consistently on fire with blazing lead guitar solos, especially noted in Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen delivers fiery organ solos that anchor tracks like Death Don't Have No Mercy and the Cryptical Envelopment jam; his keyboard work is highlighted as integral to the early Dead sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart adds glockenspiel texture on New Potato Caboose, and the drum work overall drives the high‑energy performances.
